card.title: Classification into Groups, Periods and Blocks (s, p, d, f Blocks & Metal Classifications)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The long-form table is a configuration map: **7 periods** (2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32 elements — the period number is the highest shell n being filled) and **18 groups** (same outer configuration = same family: s-block groups 1–2, p-block 13–18 counted as 10 + outer electrons, d-block 3–12 counted as s electrons + 10).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Period = highest occupied n - Group: s-block = outer e⁻; p-block = 10 + outer e⁻; d-block = s e⁻ + 10 - Elements per period: 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Period ≠ group:** period counts shells (highest n); group counts outer electrons. K and Cs share group 1 but sit in periods 4 and 6.  ·  **d-block group arithmetic:** Sc = 4s²3d¹ → 2 + 10 = group 3; Mn = 4s²3d⁵ → group 7; Zn = 4s²3d¹⁰ → group 12. Adding s + d electrons gives wrong answers.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Elements of the same group have the same number of valence electrons and hence similar chemical properties."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Fe = [Ar] 4s² 3d⁶ → period 4, group 8, d-block*** — the model answer chain: read n, read last subshell, count s electrons + 10.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: classification of elements into different groups, periods, blocks (within Classification of Elements and Periodic Table).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Reading the Table Like a Map The long-form table is not a memory chart but a **map of electronic configurations**: every period is a shell being filled, every group is a family of outer configurations, and the four blocks are the four subshell types.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Periods — the horizontal story | Period | n | Elements | Filled subshells | Type | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 1 | 2 (H, He) | 1s | **Shortest** | | 2 | 2 | 8 (Li → Ne) | 2s 2p | **Short** | | 3 | 3 | 8 (Na → Ar) | 3s 3p | **Short** | | 4 | 4 | 18 (K → Kr) | 4s 3d 4p | **Long** | | 5 | 5 | 18 (Rb → Xe) | 5s 4d 5p | **Long** | | 6 | 6 | 32 (Cs → Rn) | 6s 4f 5d 6p | **Longest** | | 7…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Row = shell, column = family, block = last subshell." Group chant: s-block count them, p-block add ten, d-block s-plus-ten. Period sizes: 2-8-8-18-18-32-32.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Name the four blocks of the periodic table, the subshell each fills, and one characteristic of each block.** — **s-block:** fills ns (groups 1–2); reactive metals forming +1/+2 ions. **p-block:** fills np (13–18); metals, metalloids, non-metals and noble gases.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): How many elements are in each of the seven periods and why do periods 4 and 5 hold 18?** — 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32. Periods 4–5 hold 18 because after the ns² pair, **ten (n−1)d electrons** fill before the six np electrons — adding a transition series of ten elements to the eight of a short period.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For "determine period/group/block" questions, show the configuration first — the marking scheme awards the configuration, then each read-off. Never skip writing the configuration.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Configuration ⇄ position:** every position question is a configuration question — highest n gives the period, the last-entering subshell gives the block, and the outer-electron count (+10 for d) gives the group.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: 7 periods (2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32 elements; period = highest n); 18 groups (s: outer e⁻; p: 10 + outer e⁻; d: s e⁻ + 10). Blocks: s (1–2), p (13–18), d (3–12, transition), f (lanthanoids/actinoids, inner-transition). Fe (Z = 26): period 4, group 8, d-block.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The table's 18-group, 7-period shape is mandated by orbital capacities: 2 + 8 + 8 + 18 + 18 + 32 + 32 = 118 elements complete seven shells — Og (Z = 118) closed period 7 in 2016.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): An element has Z = 26. Write its configuration and determine its period, group, block and name.** — Fe: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 3d⁶. Highest n = 4 → **period 4**; last electron enters 3d → **d-block**; group = s electrons + 10 = 2 + 10 = **group 8**; the element is **iron**, a…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Distinguish normal and transition elements.** — **Normal (representative) elements:** s- and p-block; their outer shell is being filled; fixed valency (= group number or 8 − group).…

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Period 4 of the periodic table contains: → B  ·  The number of groups in the long form is: → C

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Period** | Row of elements filling the same principal shell | Period 3 = n = 3 | | **Group** | Column of elements with the same valence-shell configuration | Group 17: ns²np⁵ | | **Block** | Set of groups defined by the subshell the last electron enters | p-block: np filling | | **Transition…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Worked drill — position from configuration (the exam skill) **Q: An element has Z = 26. Find its period, group, block and name.** Fe: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ **4s² 3d⁶**. - Highest n = 4 → **period 4**. - Last electron enters 3d → **d-block**. - Group = outer s electrons + 10 = 2 + 10 = **group 8** (older: VIII).…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Normal vs transition vs inner-transition elements** | Basis | Normal (s, p) | Transition (d) | Inner-transition (f) | |---|---|---|---| | Subshell filling | Outer ns or np | Penultimate (n−1)d | Antepenultimate (n−2)f | | Groups | 1–2, 13–18 | 3–12 | 3 (periods 6–7) | | Metallic character | Metals → non-metals across p | All metals | All metals | |…

rows.text: No verified PYQ located specifically for this topic; NEB 2024 3m (locate Z = 19, 20, 31, 36, 55) is anchored under topic 22 and applies here. Others are NEB-style practice.  ·  Why does period 6 contain 32 elements while period 3 contains only 8?  ·  Classify Zn as transition or non-transition and justify both readings.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why do Li and Mg resemble each other more than Li and Na do?  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Group of d-block elements:** add 10 to the outer s electrons — Fe (4s²) is group 8, not 2. The "outer electrons only" rule belongs to s/p blocks.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Zn, Cd, Hg — transition or not?** Strictly, a transition element needs a partly filled d subshell in the atom **or a common ion**; Zn²⁺/Cd²⁺/Hg²⁺ are d¹⁰, so many texts exclude them (CBSE/NEP convention lists them as exceptions).  ·  **He's block:** He ends period 1 but its configuration is 1s² — placed with group 18 (noble gases) by property, though it is formally an s-orbital filling.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (2m): Name the blocks and state which subshell each fills.** — s-block: ns (groups 1–2); p-block: np (13–18); d-block: (n−1)d (3–12, transition metals); f-block: (n−2)f (lanthanoids/actinoids, inner-transition).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Why are d-block elements called transition elements?** — They stand between the electropositive s-block and electronegative p-block, and their properties **transition** between the two: their penultimate d subshell is being filled, giving variable valency, coloured ions and catalytic behaviour.  ·  **NEB-style (3m): An element has configuration [Kr] 5s² 4d¹⁰ 5p². Determine its period, group, block and name.** — Highest n = 5 → period 5; last electron in 5p → p-block; outer electrons 5s²5p² = 4 → group 14; the element is **tin (Sn, Z = 50)**.
